subject: Geography
central_question: What drives waves, tides and ocean currents, how do these movements differ, and how do they affect coasts, climate and human activity?
in_scope_units: Horizontal and vertical movements of ocean water
Types of tides by frequency and earth-moon-sun position
banned_topics: Detailed ocean-floor relief and salinity distribution from Chapter 12 except where they control currents
Detailed atmospheric circulation beyond wind controls used here

known_pitfalls.claim: The same mass of water travels forward with a wave over long distances.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter says wave energy moves forward while water particles mainly move in small circles.

known_pitfalls.claim: Tides and surges are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Tides are regular astronomical changes; surges are irregular and meteorological.

known_pitfalls.claim: Spring tides occur only in spring.
known_pitfalls.correction: They occur when sun, moon and earth align, around new and full moon.

known_pitfalls.claim: Ocean currents are driven only by wind.
known_pitfalls.correction: Solar heating, gravity, Coriolis force and density differences also matter.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 2(iv): explain how tides are caused
NCERT Exercise 2(v): relate tides to navigation
NCERT Exercise 3(ii): explain causes of currents
NCERT Exercise 3(i): explain current effects on temperature and coastal climate
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1, 2 and 3 and Project Work on observing waves and interpreting ocean-current maps.
